prompt:
Use case: illustration-story, reference-guided revision.
Create ONE revised FIRST PAGE of the game's opening comic, horizontal 16:9. The user requests three concrete changes: the antique handled oil lantern HANGS ON THE WALL; the tiny spirit ADJUSTS A BUILT-IN LANTERN LIGHT-REDIRECTING PLATE so existing lamp light falls on PEOPLE LIVING IN THE ROOM; the page layout must be CLEARLY DIFFERENT from the other page's upper-two/lower-three layout.

REFERENCE ROLES:
Image 1 = previous origin page: retain its precise antique lantern design, watercolor quality, creamy paper, spirit identity and warm-home-to-cold-wandering story. REPLACE its tabletop lantern setting, separate handheld mirror, people-less home, and its old 2+3 panel arrangement.
Image 2 = exact character anatomy and proportions. Keep same cream flame spirit, no costume redesign.

NEW DISTINCT LAYOUT — FIVE PANELS, ARRANGEMENT 1 / 3 / 1:
A single WIDE ESTABLISHING POLYGON stretches across the TOP of the page, about 32 percent of usable height.
A MIDDLE BAND of THREE uneven oblique polygons occupies about 38 percent of usable height: left panel about 38 percent of the width, middle panel about 27 percent, right panel about 35 percent. These are sequential close scenes.
A single WIDE FINAL POLYGON spans the BOTTOM about 27 percent of usable height. Top and bottom broad scenes connect the intimate middle details.
Shared boundaries are sloped and kinked at staggered points, and the middle dividers lean in DIFFERENT directions, creating varied trapezoids/pentagons. Not a rectangular storyboard grid and not the previous two large upper panels plus three lower panels. Keep FIVE clearly enclosed panels, no extra insets.
Large uncovered ivory parchment gutters around 2.5 percent of total width, outer margin around 3 percent. Single fine sepia outlines, no heavy black bars. Subtle old vellum fibers and edge mottling, not dirty or burnt. No headings, captions, numerals, dialogue, arrows or watermark. Illustrations upright even though borders slant. Clear reading order: large top scene -> middle-left -> middle-center -> middle-right -> broad bottom scene.

ONE CONSISTENT LANTERN DESIGN:
Same compact old hand-carried oil lantern as Image 1: dull dark brown aged metal, rubbed brass highlights, arch-shaped swinging carry handle, little peaked faceted vented cap, six-sided cloudy amber glass chamber with slim protective metal ribs, low broad metal oil-reservoir base, little ordinary wick flame inside. Soot near cap and mottled glass. No electric parts. Repeat this exact handle/body/cap/base silhouette in every panel.
In the first two scenes the lantern is SUSPENDED by its arch handle from a short curved wrought-iron wall hook/bracket anchored in an aged cream-plaster wall with timber trim. The whole lantern is visibly hanging away from the wall and above the furniture. NEVER set it on a desk. Do not replace it with a fixed electric sconce; it is a portable lantern hung by its handle.
There is a small worn gap under its lower metal rim where the thumb-size spirit lives.

BUILT-IN LIGHT PLATE, CRITICAL:
The lantern has a small thin curved polished-brass reflector plate / swivelling light vane ("灯片") mounted on a tiny pivot INSIDE one side of the lantern frame, beside the lower glass opening. It is a believable part of the lantern, held by little metal brackets, and can be nudged sideways to direct the existing wick flame's light. The spirit can stand on the lower rim and push this attached plate with its hands.
NO standalone rectangular mirror, no glass shard held separately, no mirror sitting on a table. The character is specifically adjusting the lantern's OWN attached lamp plate. Show its little hinge/pivot clearly in the action closeup.
Light must visibly originate from the wick flame inside the lantern -> fall onto the polished built-in plate -> reflect outward toward a person and the person's activity. The spirit's head/chest/hands DO NOT create or shoot a beam. Warm visible dusty illumination, not a laser.

PANEL 1, TOP WIDE — A WALL LANTERN IN AN INHABITED HOME:
A warm quiet old home interior. On the LEFT/upper-left wall, the antique handled lantern hangs from the clearly visible iron hook. The tiny cream wick spirit peeks from the protected seam at the lantern base; it is tiny beside the human-size lantern.
Toward the RIGHT, an ordinary ADULT sits at an old wooden table/armchair reading an open book. A second adult farther back quietly pours water or arranges everyday household items. Modest timeless muted clothing, natural understated painterly faces, not detailed portraits; do not define family roles, add children or pets. They are calm inhabitants going about daily life.
The lantern's soft warmth reaches the reader's book and hands. A chair, bowl, cup, books and a few plants establish everyday activity without clutter. This must unmistakably be PEOPLE LIVING IN THE ROOM, not an empty decorative still life. The wall hook, suspended lantern, tiny spirit and lit human activity read in one coherent environment.

PANEL 2, MIDDLE LEFT — SPIRIT TURNS THE LANTERN PLATE:
A much closer, intimate side view of the SAME WALL-HUNG lantern's lower half, with a hint of the handle/hook above if space permits. The tiny spirit balances on the existing lower metal rim, short arms pressing or rotating the little curved brass light plate attached to its pivot beside the glass. Whole body and hands readable.
The wick flame is visible nearby INSIDE the glass, the plate catches its existing light, and a small soft golden shaft exits to the RIGHT toward the same READER'S HANDS AND OPEN BOOK, visible at the far side of the composition in a softer background. This links the gesture to a PERSON benefiting, not merely to an empty book on a desk.
Arrange the light path so it is unobstructed by the spirit's head; the spirit stands to the side of the ray. Beam origin is the wick; reflection vertex is the attached lamp plate. The plate has a definite bracket/pivot, not a free-floating mirror. Do not add light rays emerging from the body.

PANEL 3, MIDDLE CENTER — MOVING AWAY / TAKING DOWN THE LANTERN:
The SAME room now partly empty: packed unlabelled boxes, pale rectangles where pictures hung, cool daylight. A partially visible adult hand and forearm hold the lantern's arch handle just as it is lifted free of the SAME iron WALL HOOK. The now-empty hook is visible on the wall directly above it, making removal unmistakable. No whole new character portrait needed. The lantern is extinguished and cold. The tiny spirit is still sheltered at its base seam, much smaller than the human fingers. No hurt or threat, just a quiet household moving on. Same architecture as top scene.

PANEL 4, MIDDLE RIGHT — THE LOST HOME:
On the bare floor beside a packing box, the same lantern has been taken apart and left broken: low metal reservoir base, cracked amber glass panel, bent metal rib and detached cap with arch handle. Include the small attached reflector plate now resting askew within the damaged frame, maintaining the object identity. A few glass chips only. The spirit has climbed out and stands beside the broken rim, looking back. No electric cords, plugs, bulbs or ceramic desk-lamp pieces. No fire in the broken lamp and no injury. The emotional point is the loss of its familiar shelter.

PANEL 5, BOTTOM WIDE — BEGINNING TO WANDER:
A low atmospheric wide view from outside the old wooden doorway, tiny spirit walking LEFT TO RIGHT across a worn stone threshold into cloudy blue-gray dusk. The character remains thumb-size, dwarfed by door hinges, leaves and chipped stones. Its old unlit broken lantern rests far behind in the dim empty room at left, subtle but recognizable. A short ivy-covered exterior stone wall and wind-blown leaves lead to the right and into the following page's wall-walking scene. No garden gate, greenhouse or beast yet. No rain streaks; rain is only approaching. No backpack, suitcase or new accessories. Final emotion quiet loneliness and searching for shelter.
A little self-glow around the feet is allowed, but the spirit never lights the whole room or conjures useful beams.

ART / IDENTITY:
Retain the reference's watercolor granulation, thin ink contours, restrained old storybook texture, moss green and slate-blue shadows with warm candle-like amber. Rich tangible aged wood/plaster/iron/glass, not photoreal, not glossy 3D, not modern anime faces. Human figures are understated in the SAME watercolor style, no photoreal people. Strong atmospheric light/shadow and delicate illustrated object detail.
Spirit exactly matches Image 2: oversized swept-back creamy flame head, black oval eyes, tiny mouth, blue-gray mottled shade patches, short body and round small limbs, amber flame/leaf chest inset. No nose, clothes, ears, horns, wings or props. Keep same character identity and lantern identity throughout all five panels. Only one spirit per scene. Text-free horizontal comic page.
